text:
Emma: Quick sync — need to land rollout for the customer-driven tenant-gated flag by EOW. They want a per-tenant opt-in with regulatory holdback for EU. Asking for canary window, A/B splits, and fallback policy. Who can weigh in on capacity/RTO?

Raj: I can take capacity. Rough ask: start with 1% of affected tenants, expand to 5% then 20% over 48h if no errors. Need to confirm Dedicated pools won't starve other traffic.

Chris: From runtime side — 1% by tenant is doable but we should prefer traffic-slice by region + tenant to limit blast radius. Also recommend KV-prefix caching for warmed tenants.

Taylor: For A/B for quality check, propose shadow mode + 5% matched A/B on hosts that opt in, with sampling to keep tokens < 5M/day. If we see >2% semantic regressions on our eval set, auto-roll back.

Emma: Good — propose this gating flow as launch criteria: (a) zero P0 errors in 24h, (b) latency p99 < 400ms for canary tenants, (c) quality regressions <2% on the eval suite, (d) legal sign-off for EU data path. Agree?

Raj: Agree to the criteria. One ask: how do we enforce kill-switch? Need a global circuit-breaker in flag service that can immediately divert tenant traffic to the stable variant or to dedicated fallback model.

Chris: We already have a /flags/kill endpoint in control plane. Add a per-tenant soft-redirect policy: fallback to smaller model-quantized variant + log sample. Implementation: feature flag layers: tenant-override -> region-policy -> global-default. Kill flips tenant-override to fallback.

Taylor: Ops runbook for rollback: 1) flip kill-switch, 2) revert rollout percentage to 0, 3) run short smoke on affected tenants, 4) notify customers and SRE. I'll draft the runbook.

Emma: Customer asked about A/B for pricing tier sensitivity (paid vs free). Can we exempt high-pay customers from early canary? They want guaranteed SLA.

Raj: Yes — add tier gating: premium customers are on an opt-out path (they skip early canary and go to stable variant). That reduces risk but complicates rollout math. We'll need to reserve capacity.

Chris: Capacity note: reserving for premium means we should hold back 10% of Dedicated capacity as warm standby for the new variant during rollout. Otherwise latency SLOs for premium could be impacted.

Taylor: UX/Telemetry ask: include per-tenant latency + cost delta in Redwood Console dashboards for the flag. Also surface a per-tenant quality score delta (from eval prompts).

Emma: On legal/EU data path: we'd pin EU tenants to Private VPC routing during canary to reduce data residency risk. Legal to confirm, but we should design flag config to force region routing.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for feature flag "tenant-gate-x" at 2025-07-15T09:12Z. Canary slice: eu-west-1 tenants (sampled), us-west-2 tenants (1%)

Chris: Noting one more risk — model fallback variant must be compatible for function/tool calling (we have contract checkers but add a quick schema test as part of canary smoke).

Emma: Action items: (1) Taylor draft runbook + post in #eng-oncall by EOD, (2) Raj update capacity plan and reserve 10% Dedicated for warm standby, (3) Chris add schema smoke to canary pipeline, (4) Legal ping for EU VPC pin. I'll sync with customer on the phased percentages.

Taylor: I'll drop the runbook link when ready. Also propose a short A/B test of prompt paraphrases for 48h to validate quality changes before full ramp.

Raj: One more operational constraint — billing: customer requested cost cap during early rollouts. We can enforce per-tenant token caps and alert when >80% of cap. Will add to quota config.

Emma: Perfect. If no objections I'll lock the plan and schedule the canary for tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:

Chris: +1

Taylor: +1

Raj: +1

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled for 2025-07-16T08:00Z (pending runbook and capacity reservation).
